steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly coat an 11x7-inch baking dish with nonstick cooking spray.
Place potatoes in a single layer in the prepared dish, and top with onion. In a small bowl, combine melted butter, honey, mustard, salt, and pepper; drizzle over potatoes and onion.
Bake in the preheated oven for 35 minutes or until tender, stirring halfway through the cooking time.

raw_recipe.headline: Honey Roasted Red Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: These slightly sweet honey potatoes are perfect with most entrees. They are easy to bake in the oven and have great roasted, buttery taste.

video.description: Roasted red potatoes with a bit of sweetness will add delight to any entrée. It’s versatile and pairs well with savory items. A simple and tasty side that will wow your palate. Also perfect for a potluck!

review.reviewBody: HELPFUL TIPS THAT WORK: I've made this exact recipe for several years now, & have learned a few things. They take me 40-60 min in the oven. I just take a fork & occasionally poke it to see if the fork slides in easily. I use 6-8 med red potatoes, 4 large (baseball size), or about 11-12 if they're the really small (little bigger than golf ball) ones. After I quarter the potatoes, I cut those in half again to make them more bites-size esp. for my toddler who LOVES these. I find NO NEED for butter outside of PAM to grease my dish. Otherwise, it turns out GREASY! ...and I use 3T of honey and sprinkle some parsley for color. No onions if my husband is eating. Sometimes I line w/foil too because it can get sticky, otherwise a good soaking gets it all up quickly. UPDATE: It's perfect (nice glaze) w/o being too sweet, but you should mix it a few times while baking so what has become a liquid can be reapplied and the potatoes on the top aren't dry. Be sure to line these on a sheet instead of layering too because the top ones will be dry. I ALSO have to use more than a pinch of salt. Sprinkle enough so there's a little on all the potatoes or it's too bland. Broiling for the last 2-3 min. caramelizes the honey nicely. My husband & kids like ketchup on these which surprised me since they taste divine with nothing on them.

Slightly microwave or boil potatoes and then cut after cooled. I have done it with microwaving a few minutes or following the recipe with raw potato and the microwaved version is so much better. I up the mustard, salt and pepper and triple the butter sauce - so 6 T butter, 3 T honey, 1 T dry mustard, 1 or more t salt, 1/2-1 t pepper. Think the onion is a must. My family not fond of onions to eat raw - but do enjoy in cooking. I stirred every 15 minutes and cooked till browned, crisped up some. I did sprinkle parsley on the potatoes. This is very versatile - imagine you can add cayenne or other spices and herbs and change it up. Leftovers are delicious with poached eggs! If there are any left over! Thanks for the recipe

Very easy, tasty recipe! Definitely added to our list of favorites! I did double the sauce, however, and used a bit more potatoes than called for. I have also made 4 batches then put in fridge... in morning, put in Crock-pot on Low for 1 hour then warm for a couple hours and took to a pot luck lunch.... They were a hit!

Tasty!
Used 6-8 medium sized potatoes. Cut into bite sized pieces and boil in salty water for 5mins. Don't over boil. 
Double all ingredients other than potatoes.
Lay potatoes in a single layer on greased aluminum foil in a pan. Bake --> stir half way through to mix flavours. Bake 20 mins then broil 2-3mins till caramelized.
I doubled the sauce. It needed much more than a pinch of salt. Also broiled for a few minutes at the end.

Great side dish! Doubled the sauce with extra honey. Mixed well in pan. Added salt & pepper separately. Tossed halfway to coat all over again. Took 50 min. - fork tender and just browned. Foil was a must for easy cleanup.

These potatoes are exceptional! I used baby golds because I had some leftover and left out the onion. I also increased honey to 3T and baked for 40 minutes. Make sure to stir a few times while cooking. I served with Famous Butter Chicken on this site. One of my husband's favorite meals! The potatoes are so sweet they don't even need sauce!

These were so yummy! However I found I needed to add a little bit more honey, butter, dry mustard, salt and pepper after baking time since it seemed it evaporated. I also baked them for over an hour to soften them. I also smashed with the back of a large spoon. Will make again!

These were great. Running short on time I cut the potatoes into pieces and microwaved them for 10 minutes, then coated with melted butter mixture and baked. They were done in 30 min. Next time I would cut back on the butter by a few Tbsp but otherwise really good!

I used golden potatoes instead of red as that was what I had on hand. Looked gorgeous and tasted even better! Following the suggestion from other reviews, I did boil the potatoes before baking them and was very impressed by the soft, chewy texture when they came out of the oven. I will absolutely be making these again!
Did very little to change. Did cayenne pepper instead of mustard. Added lots of cut up red pepper and purple onions. Baked in oven with Titanium pot. No sticking and turned out perfect. Loved this!!
I thought it was a solid recipe! I added a little more honey to taste and it had to cook a little longer to get fork tender.
very good, double sauce
This one is okay. Not exactly a blow-out side dish, and I found them a little soggy. Still, I wouldn't kick it out of bed, and if you're not otherwise using your oven you could do worse.
These were alright. Nothing special, but it was a nice change from our usual.
We add extra honey, and absolutely love these!

I didn’t like these, but I really wanted to. I thought the honey-mustard taste would be great with bratwurst, onion, and pepper sandwiches. I used small red and golden potatoes. Yet, despite my high hopes, I could not get used to honey - which I normally love - on non-sweet potatoes. The taste improved when I mixed them with the roasted peppers and onions that fell off my sandwich. That’s my only suggestion. I thought it was a really creative idea. Just not for me.
Easy to make and great break from fried potatoes.
I used Idaho potatoes and cut them in bite-size pieces. I didn't add as much dry mustard, just sprinkled some in, because my daughter doesn't like mustard. I loved them. I will be making them again
Easy. Also, makes great left overs.
